subject: Energy
title: Entropy and the Second Law
description: Learn Entropy and the Second Law in one minute.

hook.text: You can turn all your work into heat—but you can never turn all your heat back into work. That's the second law.

buildup.text: Entropy measures disorder—and in any real process, the total entropy of the universe always increases.

discovery.text: That's why hot coffee cools down and never spontaneously reheats—heat spreads out, and entropy rises.

twist.text: The second law explains why perpetual motion machines are impossible—some energy always becomes unusable waste heat.

climax.text: Arthur Eddington called it the supreme law of nature—if your theory violates it, there's no hope.

punchline.text: Energy is conserved—but its quality always degrades.

quiz.question: What does the second law say about entropy?
